newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian hostages and wounded Albanian fly to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Italian hostages and wounded Albanian fly to Italy.

text.p: A military helicopter on Tuesday evacuated four Italian doctors and a wounded gunman whose comrades in Albania had taken them hostage demanding that he be flown to Italy for medical treatment, the foreign ministry said.
"The emergency is over. The four Italians with the wounded Albanian are flying back by helicopter to Bari," a spokesman from the foreign ministry's crisis unit told Reuters.

The doctors, working for an Italian Red Cross relief mission in the southern rebel-held city of Vlore, were taken hostage earlier on Tuesday by Albanian rebels. "They were forced at gunpoint to take the wounded man to Italy for treatment," the spokesman said.

The ANSA news agency, in a report from the Albanian capital Tirana, quoted one of the doctors, Paolo Cherubino, as saying the wounded man had been shot in the head during an incident on Monday in which three Albanian police officers died.
The spokesman said the Albanian man was in a serious condition and would be treated at a hospital in Bari, across the southern Adriatic from Albania.
The four doctors were part of a mission providing medical care to Albanians in the south of the country, which has seen some of the worst violence in the Balkan country.
